item.title: Workers, Cloudflare CLI - Cloudflare CLI (cf) 1.0 release candidate
item.description:
Cloudflare CLI (cf) 1.0.0-rc.1 is a release candidate for cf 1.0. cf has been in beta since late September. This is the release we recommend you try on your own projects, and we want your feedback before 1.0.

To install or update to the latest release:

npm install --global cf@latest
yarn global add cf@latest
pnpm add --global cf@latest
bun add --global cf@latest

What is stable

We expect the following features to remain stable to cf 1.0:

  • The cloudflare.config.ts configuration format.
  • The Build Output format that cf build writes and cf deploy reads.
  • The commands that create, develop, build, and deploy projects, including cf init, cf dev, cf build, cf deploy, cf previews deploy, and cf workers versions create.
  • The large majority of commands generated from the Cloudflare API and used in the beta.

A small number of less commonly used API commands may still change before 1.0. cf generates these commands from the Cloudflare API schema, so their call path may still change before 1.0.

Upgrade from a beta

This release moves Build Output to version 1, in .cloudflare/output/v1/. cf deploy will automatically create a new build on first run in this location.

The release candidate also moves to caret (^) version ranges for its dependencies, requiring:

  • @cloudflare/vite-plugin 2.0.0-rc.0 or later, for projects that build with Vite.
  • Wrangler 4.163.0 or later, for legacy projects that build with Wrangler.

1.0.0-rc.1 renames a few generated API commands without aliases. For example, cf workers secrets bulk is now cf workers secrets bulk-edit. For the full list, refer to the release notes ↗︎.

If you last updated early in the beta, these earlier changes may also affect you:

  • Prompts, progress, and status messages are written to stderr. Stdout holds only command output, so scripts that read messages from stdout must read stderr instead.
  • Commands generated from camelCase or snake_case API names use kebab-case. For example, cf accounts billing getCredits is now cf accounts billing get-credits.
  • cf previews deploy takes the Preview name as --preview-name instead of a positional argument.
  • Commands run with --local store state in the project's .cloudflare/state directory.
  • cf no longer saves your account choice between runs. Set accountId in cloudflare.config.ts or CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID to skip the prompt.
  • Streaming tail consumers move to experimental.streamingTailConsumers in cloudflare.config.ts.
  • Destructive commands run without a terminal exit with an error unless you pass --force.
  • cf supports the latest versions of the Node.js LTS releases and the latest active release of Node.js.

Stream live logs

cf observability tail streams live logs and other observability events as newline-delimited JSON. Select a Worker with --worker, a zone and its subdomains with --zone, or every event in the account with --all. Narrow the results with --filters, as inline JSON or from a file:

Worker events require Workers Logs to be turned on for the Worker. For filter shapes and examples, run cf observability tail --help.

What changed during the beta

Deploy

  • Deploy a directory of static assets with cf deploy ./dist. cf skips the build step and creates an assets-only Worker.
  • cf deploy --no-provision fails when a binding has no resource ID, instead of creating a new resource.
  • cf deploy --force deploys when the Worker was last deployed through the API, or when its remote configuration conflicts with your local Build Output.
  • Redeploying no longer removes secrets that you added outside cloudflare.config.ts.
  • Stack traces from deployed Workers show project paths such as src/index.ts.
  • Python Workers with vendored packages deploy correctly.
  • cf deploy applies SSH settings for Containers managed by Durable Objects.
  • cf deploy --dry-run shows the project setup changes it would make, without making them.
  • Set CLOUDFLARE_DEPENDENCIES_INSTRUMENTATION=false to stop uploading package dependency metadata with each deployment.

Develop

  • cf init creates new Worker projects with Vite+, including checks, formatting, and tests that run in the Workers runtime.
  • cf dev and cf build run the Vite or Vite+ executable installed in your project, including dependencies hoisted in a workspace.
  • cf dev passes arguments such as --port and --host to your framework's development server.
  • cf dev --profile <name> passes the selected authentication profile to your development server.
  • cf dev, cf build, and cf deploy offer to run cf migrate when they find a Wrangler configuration file.
  • On Windows, Ctrl+C exits cleanly when your framework runs through npm, Wrangler and Vite start without spawn EFTYPE errors, and cf d1 migrations create rejects names that Windows cannot store.
  • cf init approves the build scripts that pnpm 11 and later block by default, so installation succeeds.

Sign in and accounts

  • Pass --temporary-account to create a short-lived account without signing in. cf prints a URL you can use to claim the account.
  • cf auth login summarizes the scopes you granted, and cf auth scopes lists them by product.
  • cf auth whoami, also available as cf whoami, prints a short summary in a terminal and full JSON for scripts and agents.
  • cf auth login now uses the system keyring where available.
  • Long-running commands, such as cf observability tail, refresh an expired OAuth login instead of failing.
  • cf auth whoami reports the status of scoped API tokens correctly.
  • Set CLOUDFLARE_API_HEADERS to send custom headers with API requests.

API commands

  • Every command accepts --dry-run to preview what it would do and it redacts sensitive fields in request previews.
  • cf checks --body input before it asks you to sign in or confirm, and rejects array bodies larger than the API allows instead of splitting them across several requests.
  • More request fields are available as flags, including JSON objects and maps, arrays of objects, and file uploads. For example, cf pages deployments create --worker-js @./_worker.js and cf ai to-markdown --files @first.html @second.pdf.
  • Error outputs have been improved with additional messages the API returns, such as the names of missing parameters.
  • cf workers commands accept --worker to select a Worker.
  • --zone finds zones by name in accounts with many zones.
  • cf tunnels quick-start --allowed-mail limits a temporary tunnel to the email addresses and domains you allow.

Scripts and agents

  • cf --version prints only the version number.
  • Shell completions and cf tools list every flag a command accepts.
  • cf cli search has reranked cf deploy and other key commands to improve their ranking for static site and Pages deployment searches.
  • cf docs search finds Cloudflare documentation from the terminal.

Send feedback

To report a bug or tell us what is missing, open an issue in the cf repository ↗︎. For every change in each release, refer to the Cloudflare CLI release notes ↗︎.

item.title: Workers, Cloudflare CLI - Serve a Worker's static assets from a URL path like /blog/
item.description:
You can now serve your Worker's static assets from a URL path prefix, such as example.com/blog/, without changing your build output.

Previously, to serve assets from /blog/, you had to nest your files in a matching blog directory. Now, set assets.base_path in your Wrangler configuration file, or worker.assets.basePath in cloudflare.config.ts, and keep your files at the root of your asset directory.

Use Wrangler 4.148.0 ↗︎ or later. With cloudflare.config.ts, use cf 1.0.0-beta.13 ↗︎ or later.

For example, this configuration serves your built assets from /blog/:

The following content appears twice: first for the Cloudflare CLI (cf), then for Wrangler. Use cf for new projects. In an existing project, use the CLI that the project already uses.

Cloudflare CLI

Wrangler

Requests to /blog/ serve dist/index.html, and requests to /blog/posts/post1 serve dist/posts/post1.html. Requests outside /blog/ do not match your static assets and run your Worker, if it has one.

Paths in _headers, _redirects, and run_worker_first use the full public path, including /blog. If you build with the Cloudflare Vite plugin, also set Vite's base option to /blog/.

For more information, refer to Serving a subdirectory.

item.title: Workers, Cloudflare CLI - Wrangler and cf now upload source maps by default
item.description:
From Wrangler 4.150.0, wrangler deploy, wrangler versions upload, and wrangler preview generate and upload source maps by default. You no longer need to set upload_source_maps to get stack traces with your original file names and line numbers.

cf deploy also uploads source maps by default. With the Cloudflare Vite plugin 1.64.0 or later, Worker builds generate source maps by default, and cf deploy uploads every source map in the build output.

Remapped stack traces show up in Workers Logs, real-time logs, Tail Workers, and Workers Issues. Source maps are applied after your Worker runs, so they don't affect CPU time, bundle size, or cold starts.

If your Worker uses a custom build, Wrangler uploads any external source maps it finds. Maps it can't resolve, such as inline data: source maps, are skipped instead of failing the upload. Set upload_source_maps to true if you'd prefer the upload to fail.

To opt out with Wrangler, set upload_source_maps to false:

To opt out with cf or the Cloudflare Vite plugin, set build.sourcemap to false for your Worker's Vite environment. Refer to Disable source maps.

item.title: Workers, Cloudflare CLI - Test Cron Triggers with Local Explorer
item.description:
Local Explorer can now send one-off Cron Trigger invocations to a Worker's scheduled() handler during local development. This removes the need to construct request URLs when testing handler behavior.

Start your local development server with cf dev, wrangler dev, or the Cloudflare Vite plugin. Open /cdn-cgi/local/explorer on the server URL and select Cron Triggers.

The browser interface supports the following tasks:

  • Invoke configured cron expressions
  • Build ad hoc expressions
  • Set reusable scheduled times
  • Inspect outcomes and noRetry() status

Ad hoc triggers and scheduled time presets stay in your browser. They do not change cloudflare.config.ts, your Wrangler configuration, or deployed Cron Triggers. Local development does not run cron schedules automatically.

Full logs and traces are available in the development session that owns the Worker when that session has Observability turned on.

item.title: Workers, Cloudflare CLI - Search Cloudflare documentation with the Cloudflare CLI
item.description:
Cloudflare CLI 1.0.0-beta.16 includes cf docs search, so you and your coding agent can find Cloudflare documentation without leaving the terminal. Search for guides, tutorials, and examples across Cloudflare products.

To install or update to the latest release:

npm install --global cf@latest
yarn global add cf@latest
pnpm add --global cf@latest
bun add --global cf@latest

Describe what you want to do, or ask a question:

The command searches live Cloudflare documentation and returns up to five ranked JSON results. Each result includes a title, description, and documentation URL. An Internet connection is required.

Agents can parse the results and fetch a complete page as Markdown. For example, use jq to select the first result, then request its URL with the Accept: text/markdown header:

This release also standardizes generated command names to kebab-case. For example, cf accounts billing getCredits becomes cf accounts billing get-credits. For the full list of breaking command and flag changes, refer to the Cloudflare CLI release notes ↗︎.

For more information, refer to Find Cloudflare documentation with a coding agent.

item.title: Workers, Cloudflare CLI - Cloudflare CLI is now in beta
item.description:
The Cloudflare CLI, cf, is now in beta. cf is one command-line interface for the public Cloudflare API and for Workers projects. Use it to manage zones, DNS, storage, and security settings, and to create, develop, and deploy Workers, without switching between tools.

Install cf globally, then sign in:

npm install --global cf
yarn global add cf
pnpm add --global cf
bun add --global cf

With cf, you can:

  • Manage resources across Cloudflare. More than 2,900 commands cover the public Cloudflare API, and most print their results as JSON.
  • Create and deploy Workers. cf init creates a project that uses cloudflare.config.ts, a typed configuration file. cf dev, cf build, and cf deploy develop, build, and deploy it.
  • Move from Wrangler. cf migrate converts a Wrangler configuration file to cloudflare.config.ts. You can also run cf resource commands in an existing Wrangler project without migrating it.
  • Work with coding agents. cf cli search finds the command for a task from a plain-language description, so an agent can find and run commands without prior knowledge of cf.

cf is in beta. Commands, configuration, and Build Output can change before the stable release.

To get started, refer to Install and sign in. To move an existing project, refer to Migrate a Wrangler project.
